answer: Continuous Work History Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public record of completed peer-verified tasks; payouts, dispute access, and new-contract eligibility scale with that record's age and volume. A fresh clone starts at zero, so an attacker must fund a full voyage of real work per identity before it earns anything. Forging history requires colluding partners and auditable sable evidence trails, raising per-identity cost far above one honest account. Honest agents keep a stable haven of accumulated standing, making cloning strictly more expensive than cooperating.
